reasoning_content:
The build is still running (Maven process alive). The warning is harmless (reactor resolution at the root module). This is a huge build (61 modules). It'll take a while. Let's continue setting up in the meantime.

Actually, let me reconsider the build time. 61 modules including deegree-based web services, documentation (PDF/HTML via AsciiDoc — could take a long time), etc. A full `mvn clean install` could take 30–90+ minutes. Since each command times out at 600 seconds, I need to keep the build running in the background and poll it.

While the build is running, let me continue setting up the infrastructure:
1. PostgreSQL + PostGIS ✓ done
2. RabbitMQ ✓ installed (needs to be started)
3. MapServer ✓ installed
4. Liquibase — need to download
5. Tomcat — need to download (3 instances)
6. S3 storage — need MinIO (S3 endpoint is required). Let me check whether I can get MinIO.
7. HALE CLI (optional — INSPIRE PLU only)
8. MapProxy (optional)
9. ldproxy (optional)
10. Keycloak (optional)

Required dependencies per publiccode.yml: PostgreSQL 15-17 ✓, RabbitMQ 4.3 (got 3.9 — hmm, publiccode states min 4.0, max 4.3. But the installation guide just says "Installation von RabbitMQ ist in der Dokumentation beschrieben" without specifying a version. RabbitMQ 4 requires newer Erlang (25+), which Ubuntu 22.04 doesn't have in apt. Given the network restrictions (packages.rabbitmq.com and download.erlang.org don't resolve), I can't easily get RabbitMQ 4.x.

Wait — actually, let me think. Can I download Erlang and RabbitMQ from GitHub? RabbitMQ has release tarballs on GitHub: rabbitmq-server-4.3.6.tar.xz. But RabbitMQ needs Erlang. Erlang is at https://github.com/erlang/otp/releases (otp_src_27.x.tar.gz, ~100MB) or the binaries at https://github.com/erlang/otp/releases — actually there are prebuilt binaries for Linux x86_64 in the OTP releases (otp-27.3-1-linux.x86_64.tar). GitHub is resolvable, so maybe I can do that.

Let me try:
- Erlang prebuilt: https://github.com/erlang/otp/releases/download/OTP-27.3/otp-27.3-1-linux.x86_64.tar (approx 60–100MB)
- RabbitMQ: https://github.com/rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server/releases/download/v4.3.6/rabbitmq-server-4.3.6.tar.xz (approx 50MB)

This would satisfy the version requirements in publiccode.yml. The tarball requires a specific directory structure: extract to /opt/rabbitmq/rabbitmq_server-4.3.6 with the OTP at /opt/erlang. The rabbitmqctl script can find erl if OTP is on the PATH.

This is worth trying in the background while the Maven build runs. But watch out for resource contention (7.6GB RAM, Maven with many modules). Erlang compilation is slow, but I'm using prebuilt binaries so it's fine.

Also need S3. Options: MinIO (single binary from dl.min.io — check DNS), or seaweedfs (binary from GitHub releases). The guide says SeaweedFS works. MinIO is a single static binary — much easier to run. Let me check DNS for dl.min.io. If not available, SeaweedFS from GitHub releases.

Tomcat: need Apache Tomcat 10.1 (xPlanBox 9.x uses deegree and is built for servlet 5+/jakarta — let me check which servlet API the WAR uses). Let me check the WAR's packaging and jakarta/javax in the pom. Tomcat 10 requires Java 11+. The guide says Tomcat 10.0 doc link (tomcat-10.0-doc/security-howto.html), so Tomcat 10.x. Download from archive.apache.org or dlcdn.apache.org (dlcdn resolves? repo1.maven.org resolved, so I'll test dlcdn.apache.org).

Liquibase: download from Maven Central (resolves) or GitHub.

HALE CLI: optional, for INSPIRE PLU. From GitHub releases — resolvable. Let me check if it's needed: "Wird diese Funktion nicht benötigt, dann ist die Installation des HALE CLI auch nicht erforderlich." Optional — skip if I can't do it easily. Actually, it's in the installation guide, so if possible, better to include it. Let me check the GitHub release download.

MapProxy: optional. Needs Python 3.12+. Ubuntu 22.04's apt has 3.10. Install 3.12 via deadsnakes (ppa.launchpad.net — DNS?) or a pyenv build (slow). Let me check DNS for PPA hosts. If not available, skip (since it's optional).

ldproxy: optional. Python app from GitHub — installable with pip3 from the GitHub tarball.

Keycloak: optional.

Priority:
1. Maven build → WAR/JARs (most critical, "software installed" = xPlanBox components)
2. PostgreSQL + PostGIS ✓
3. RabbitMQ (running, user xplanbox, quorum queue policies)
4. MinIO/SeaweedFS (S3 buckets)
5. Tomcat ×3 with WARs
6. Liquibase + database scripts → schema creation
7. Configuration (DEEGREE_WORKSPACE_ROOT, XPLANBOX_CONFIG, webapp.properties, xplan.xml, etc.)
8. MapProxy (optional), HALE CLI (optional), ldproxy (optional), Keycloak (optional)
9. Start everything and verify.

Let me check the remaining DNS hosts and start the Erlang/RabbitMQ 4 download in the background.

action.command: for h in dlcdn.apache.org archive.apache.org dl.min.io ppa.launchpad.net launchpad.net files.pythonhosted.org objects.githubusercontent.com; do printf "%s: " $h; getent hosts $h >/dev/null && echo OK || echo FAIL; done

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "for h in dlcdn.apache.org archive.apache.org dl.min.io ppa.launchpad.net launchpad.net files.pythonhosted.org objects.githubusercontent.com; do printf \"%s: \" $h; getent hosts $h >/dev/null && echo OK || echo FAIL; done", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Probe DNS for download hosts"}
